records.statement: Origin, insertion and joint crossing provide a structural basis for describing a muscle's plausible actions, but anatomy alone does not quantify its contribution during an exercise.
records.applies_to: SportRX training-anatomy records and educational movement explanations.
allowed_language: This muscle crosses the elbow and can contribute to elbow flexion.
Its attachments make the listed joint actions anatomically plausible.
disallowed_language: This anatomy proves that the exercise maximally activates the muscle.
Origin and insertion identify the best hypertrophy exercise.
The catalogue can diagnose a weak muscle.
records.limitations: Muscle contribution depends on joint position, external load, technique, task and individual anatomy; these records are concise educational summaries.

records.statement: A muscle crossing two joints can change length and mechanical contribution when either joint position changes, so a movement label alone is not a complete training description.
records.applies_to: Biarticular muscles represented in SportRX, including biceps brachii, triceps long head, rectus femoris, hamstrings and gastrocnemius.
allowed_language: Knee position changes gastrocnemius length because it crosses the knee and ankle.
Hip position is relevant when interpreting rectus femoris or hamstring exercises.
disallowed_language: One joint position completely isolates a biarticular muscle.
Anatomy alone proves a regional hypertrophy advantage.
SportRX can infer safe joint positions for pain.
records.limitations: This is a structural interpretation boundary, not a direct measurement of force, activation, hypertrophy or individual tolerance.

records.statement: Prime-mover, synergist, antagonist and stabilizer roles are task-dependent descriptions and should not be converted into fixed exercise rankings or identical set credit.
records.applies_to: SportRX muscle coverage, movement patterns and representative exercise explanations.
allowed_language: The triceps contributes to horizontal pressing while the pectorals remain the primary atlas region.
A muscle may act as a mover in one task and a stabilizer in another.
disallowed_language: Every participating muscle receives the same hypertrophy dose.
A stabilizer never needs direct training.
The listed prime mover is the only active muscle.
records.limitations: Role labels simplify coordination and do not replace biomechanical measurement, EMG interpretation or longitudinal hypertrophy evidence.
